question.prompt: The least value of the function \(ax^2+bx+c\) with \(a>0\) is:

solutions.explanation:
Because \(a>0\), rewriting the expression as a positive multiple of a square will reveal its least value. For real \(x\), completing the square gives
\[
ax^2+bx+c
=a\left(x+\frac{b}{2a}\right)^2+c-\frac{b^2}{4a}.
\]
The square is nonnegative, so
\[
ax^2+bx+c\ge c-\frac{b^2}{4a}
=\frac{4ac-b^2}{4a}.
\]
Equality occurs at \(x=-\frac{b}{2a}\), where the square vanishes. All denominators are nonzero because \(a>0\). Thus the least value is \(\boxed{\frac{4ac-b^2}{4a}}\), choice D.
solutions.title: Complete the square
